baseline-first.remarks: Both extractors struggle with the linearized text layer's lack of structural grouping, causing attribute bleeding between adjacent schedule items (e.g., Paint attributes binding to Tile entities). Set B's attempt at higher recall results in a disproportionately high false positive rate.

variant-first.note: Set B is preferred because it contains significantly fewer incorrect claims (3 vs 10), adhering to the preference for precision over recall. While Set A captures more correct equipment data, its high rate of misbound attributes in the finish schedule (e.g., assigning paint colors to tiles) reduces trustworthiness. variant-first.remarks: Both sets suffer from row-alignment errors in the Finish and Furniture schedules (e.g. claiming Porcelain Tile has Laminate dimensions). Set A's broader coverage of Equipment and Plumbing is valuable but outweighed by the volume of hallucinated/misbound finish data.
